chunks: A man asked Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said to him:
O son of the cousin of the best of Allah’s creation, what is the meaning of the first sajdah (prostration)?

He said: “Its interpretation is: O Allah, indeed from it You created us, meaning from the earth. The interpretation of raising your head is: and from it You brought us out. The interpretation of the second sajdah is: and to it You return us. And raising your head is: and from it You will bring us out another time.”

key_terms.السَّجْدَةِ: the prostration in salat (prayer), here explained symbolically
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the earth, from which human beings were created and to which they return
key_terms.تَارَةً أُخْرَى: another time, meaning the final rising again
key_terms.تُخْرِجُنَا: You bring us forth, referring to emergence into life and resurrection
key_terms.تُعِيدُنَا: You return us, referring to death and burial in the earth

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the two sajdahs in salat (prayer) according to Imam Ali عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the symbolic meaning of the two sajdahs in salat (prayer). The first sajdah and rising from it recall human creation from the earth and emergence into life, while the second sajdah and rising from it recall return to the earth in death and resurrection from it once more.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.930 - A man asked The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) saying:
"O’ son of the cousin of the best of Allah’s (swt) creation, what is the meaning of the first sajdah (prostration)?"

Imam Ali (as) replied: "Its meaning is, 'O’ Allah (swt), from it (the earth) You created us,' referring to being created from the earth. The meaning of raising your head is 'and from it, You brought us forth.' The meaning of the second sajdah is 'and to it, You shall return us,' and raising your head again means 'and from it, You shall bring us forth another time.'"
